pageCache.text:
Our Value this term is Courage
Welcome to Kingsholm C of E Primary School and Nursery
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Kingsholm C of E Primary School and Nursery and to our website.
Kingsholm Church of England Primary School and Nursery is a true inner-city school in the heart of Gloucester. As a Church school, we have a strong Christian ethos and are linked to St Catharine’s Church and Gloucester Cathedral. Our core values are Respect, Love and Perseverance.
At our school, we believe that everyone matters, and every child deserves to feel happy, safe, and valued. Creating a sense of belonging is at the heart of everything we do, and we work tirelessly to ensure that our school is a place where children can thrive academically, socially, and emotionally.
We are proud to champion the needs of our children and their families, providing an inclusive, nurturing environment where every individual is supported to achieve their full potential. Whether it’s through our dedicated teaching, our vibrant enrichment, or our strong pastoral care, we are committed to ensuring that each child feels seen, heard, and empowered.
It is a privilege to serve this wonderful community, and I am deeply grateful for the trust and partnership of our families. Together, we are building a school that is not only a place of learning but also a second home – a place where children are inspired, challenged, and prepared for a bright future.
Thank you for visiting our website, and we hope it gives you a glimpse into the spirit and values of our school.
If you require paper copies of any information on our school's website, please contact us and copies will be provided free of charge.

Headteacher's Message
Dear Parents/Carers,
We have made it! Autumn term 1 is done and we can all look forward to the October half term and the upcoming Christmas Term.
This has been my first Autumn Term at Kingsholm and once again I have been amazed at the wonderful opportunities the staff create for our children.
We have seen everything from: Theatre productions, birds of prey, sports fixtures, clubs, Break the Rules day and so much more. The staff work incredibly hard to provide a rich and varied education for all.
Next term is packed so look out for dates: Time to Talk Evenings, Nativity and Christingle to name a few.
Last week we had a visit from an OFSTED Inspector who was asked to review the progress the school had made recently, and I wanted to celebrate some of her comments to really highlight how the school is continually striving to improve:
The school is an inclusive, nurturing environment. The highly structured and well-established routines help pupils feel safe, happy and ready to learn.
Pupils who struggle to come into school are given sensitive, meaningful support.
Classrooms are calm and purposeful. Relationships between adults and pupils are warm and respectful.
Expectations for behaviour are high and applied consistently, with reasonable adjustments for pupils who need support.
Pupils behaved well in all lessons visited.
The work done to develop the curriculum since the inspection is impressive.
Phonics was taught consistently well in all sessions visited.
Have a wonderful break

Reminders…..
Please check your child's hair on a regular basis
Head lice can make your head feel itchy.
The only way to be sure someone has head lice is by finding live lice.
You can do this by combing their hair with a special fine-toothed comb (detection comb). You can buy these online or at pharmacies.
How to get rid of head lice
Treat head lice as soon as you spot them. You can treat head lice without seeing a GP.
Check everyone you live with, or have close contact with, and start treating anyone who has head lice on the same day.
There's no need to keep your child off school if they have head lice. You do not need to wash your laundry on a hot wash.
Wet combing
Lice and nits can be removed by wet combing.
You can buy a special fine-toothed comb (detection comb) online or from pharmacies to remove head lice and nits.
There may be instructions on the pack, but usually you:
It usually takes about 10 minutes to comb short hair, and 20 to 30 minutes for long, frizzy or curly hair. When you've finished combing the hair, comb through all the hair again for a second time.
Do wet combing on days 1, 5, 9 and 13 to catch any newly hatched head lice. Check again that everyone's hair is free of lice on day 17.
wash hair with ordinary shampoo
Medicated lotions and sprays
If wet combing has not worked or is not suitable, you could try a medicated lotion or spray. These kill head lice in all types of hair, and you can buy them from pharmacies, supermarkets or online.
Head lice should die within a day. Some lotions and sprays come with a comb to remove dead lice and eggs.
Some treatments need to be repeated after a week to kill any newly hatched lice.
Check the pack to see if they're OK for you or your child to use, and how to use them.
If lotions or sprays do not work, speak to a pharmacist about other treatments.
Treatments that are not recommended for head lice
Some treatments are not recommended because they're unlikely to work.
products containing permethrin
head lice "repellents"
electric combs for head lice
Wet combing video
The charity Community Hygiene Concern has a video about wet combing for head lice.

Meet the Governors
What do Kingsholm C of E Primary School Governors do?
Here at Kingsholm C of E Primary School and Nursery Governors are an important part of `Our Kingsholm Family' and all our work is guided by the school's vision Everyone matters.
All schools must, by law, have a Governing Board to provide oversight and accountability of the school's life. To do this we work together - our decisions are joint ones, no individual governors make decisions on their own. This is called ‘collective responsibility’.
The Governing Board holds the main responsibility for the financial management of the school, and we work with the senior management team to make major decisions, including how the school is staffed and difficult decisions, such as how to balance resources. The governors are also responsible for appointing the Headteacher and the Deputy Headteacher.
So, we have a key strategic role. We look at the ‘whole school picture’. We focus on setting the aims and objectives of the school and set policies and targets to achieve these.
Being a governor is a voluntary role and we know it needs a considerable amount of time and commitment. We are keen to find ways to help parents join us, by looking at different ways to help you fit the role into your busy work and home lives. We want our governing body to reflect the whole of our community.
The government also recognises that governors have an important role to play in school life and ‘by law, employers must give employees who serve on maintained school boards ‘reasonable time off’ to carry out their duties.’ Please see below to find out more details about this.
We currently have several Governors who work full time, are parents and successfully carry out their Governor duties. As we all work together as a team, we make sure that tasks are shared out, so that no-one should feel that the role is too much. New governors are also supported by other members of the Governing Body.
However, our main reason for being governors is that we want to ensure that ‘life in all its fullness’ is achievable for all our children – we want our pupils to see and reach their full potential.
It is a very rewarding role – you get to play a part in helping make Kingsholm a fantastic school and be part of the many exciting projects that happen here. Some of our recent work has been in seeing the extension of the school, regaining the nursery, overseeing the OPAL scheme, and appointing our new Headteacher and Deputy Headteachers. All of these projects will have long-lasting positive effects on the lives of the children who come to Kingsholm.
All school governors are subject to an enhanced DBS check before taking up their appointment.
For further information about becoming a school governor, you might like to look at this link
https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/education-and-learning/become-a-school-governor/
To contact the Clerk to Governors, please email clerk@kingsholm.gloucs.sch.uk

Our Governors
Headteacher & ExOfficio
Having been in education for over 25 years I have seen a huge amount of change and experienced a wide variety of systems and schools. I have worked within the Gloucestershire Local Authority for the entirety of my teaching career (spending time in Stroud, Forest of Dean, Cheltenham and Gloucester). I have worked in large schools, small schools, Church Schools and non-denominational schools but Kingsholm is by far the largest school that I have led as a Headteacher.
My leadership career has allowed me to have the pleasure of leading multiple schools from a 'Requires Improvement' position to 'Good' under the previous OFSTED framework and help ensure that the highest quality education is delivered to all young people.
I am passionate about making education a fun and engaging process and developing a life-long love of learning. I truly believe that Primary school should be about making memories and preparing children for the next stage in their journey - wherever that may take them.
Working at Kingsholm has brought me full circle in my leadership journey - having completed my NPQH placement here some 15 years ago under the leadership of Jan Buckland. The school has the most incredible children, serves a brilliant community and has passionate and committed staff that really do make a difference. For me, that is what education is all about!
Co-opted Governor & Chair of Governors
Mrs Sophie Kingscote
I have been a governor at Kingsholm Primary School for over ten years and currently serve as Chair of Governors. Both of my children attended Kingsholm, which gives me a strong personal connection to the school and its community.
I work as a secondary school teacher, bringing experience from across the education sector to my role. I am passionate about inclusion and ensuring that every child feels supported, valued and able to thrive. As Chair, I am committed to working with staff and fellow governors to help the school provide the very best opportunities for all pupils.

Kingsholm C of E Primary School and Nursery Virtual Tour
Nursery and Reception at Kingsholm
St Catharines Vicar - Jo Pestell
About Our School
We are a large 3 form entry Primary School. Kingsholm C of E Primary School is situated in the heart of the City of Gloucester.
We are a member of the Gloucester Schools Partnership which is dedicated to helping raise the achievement of all children in Gloucester's schools network.
Our buildings are set in grounds of some 6 acres that provide both space and a full range of outdoor activities for the children.
We are very proud of our school environment and have many different areas for the children to learn in. The spiritual area is somewhere the children can go to reflect and learn in a peaceful and relaxing location.
The field, playground and MUGA offer wide open spaces to play and learn in and our classrooms are designed to maximise our learning experiences.
We have a wildlife area with a pond and hide, an allotment with a greenhouse made out of plastic bottles and two fantastic willow sculptures.
We are a National Advocacy schools for the National Education Trust hosting a yearly conference here.
We have a cooking area, excellent computing resources and a fantastic sound and lighting system in the main hall for live performances.
We also have a chargeable Breakfast Club and After School Club which runs everyday. Our very popular Walking Bus collects children from their homes every morning.
We are within walking distance of many local attractions eg. the Cathedral, the Docks, Gloucester's museums and the GL1 Leisure Centre. We use these resources, and more, to enrich the childrens' curriculum giving them many first hand experiences.
We are very proud to have close links with our close neighbours, Gloucester Rugby Club. The school also raises considerable funds by acting as a car park on match days.
